title: Evaluation equivalence for modules on a one-point ringed space
statement: Let (Y, O_Y) be a ringed space whose underlying space has exactly one point. Put A = Gamma(Y,O_Y). For the category Mod(O_Y) of sheaves of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], evaluation on the whole space Gamma(Y,-) [def-sc-ringed-space-module-cohomology] is an equivalence Mod(O_Y) -> Mod(A). No nonzero-ring hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tags 009A (4) and 006U; Section 20.44, Tag 0B6A, one-point module identification used for derived global sections.

proof.text: Every open of a singleton is the whole space or the empty open. The sheaf condition for the empty cover makes the underlying abelian group of a module sheaf on the empty open terminal, hence zero.

For a module M over A = Gamma(Y,O_Y), construct the presheaf with sections PLift(x in U) -> M, where x is the unique point. For each proof x in U, the inclusion Y into U transports the O_Y(U)-action to A and then to M. Restrictions precompose membership proofs. The scalar compatibility follows from functoriality of the ring restriction maps. On a covering, choose a member containing x when the union contains x. Compatibility on intersections identifies the values there, giving a unique gluing. If the union excludes x, all section functions have empty domain and the gluing is unique. This is a module sheaf, and evaluation at the unique membership proof gives an A-linear isomorphism of its global sections with M, proving essential surjectivity.

Given an A-linear map between the global sections of two module sheaves, extend it by the same map on the whole space and zero on the empty open. For a restriction between whole-space opens, naturality is the identity restriction law. If the target open is empty, its module is zero by step 1, so naturality holds. The remaining opposite-direction case is impossible. Thus evaluation is full. If two module-sheaf morphisms have equal global components, they agree on the whole space and on the empty open by its zero module, hence are equal; evaluation is faithful. Together with step 2 this proves IsEquivalence.
